questions.questionText: Meiosis produces daughter cells that are:
questions.explanation: Meiosis reduces chromosome number by half, producing four haploid gametes (n) from one diploid parent cell (2n).

questions.questionText: How many daughter cells are produced in meiosis?
questions.explanation: Meiosis consists of two rounds of division (Meiosis I and II), producing four genetically distinct haploid daughter cells.

questions.questionText: Crossing over occurs during:
questions.explanation: During Prophase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes pair up and exchange segments of DNA (crossing over), increasing genetic variation.

questions.questionText: The main purpose of meiosis is to produce:
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces gametes (sperm and egg cells) that combine during fertilisation to maintain the diploid chromosome number.

questions.questionText: In meiosis I, homologous chromosomes:
questions.explanation: In Meiosis I, homologous chromosome pairs (one from each parent) align and separate into different cells, reducing chromosome number.

questions.questionText: Independent assortment of chromosomes occurs during:
questions.explanation: During Metaphase I, homologous chromosome pairs align randomly at the metaphase plate, independently assorting maternal and paternal chromosomes.

questions.questionText: Synapsis is:
questions.explanation: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes during Prophase I, forming structures called bivalents or tetrads.

questions.questionText: A tetrad consists of:
questions.explanation: A tetrad (bivalent) is formed when two homologous chromosomes (each with two sister chromatids) align during Prophase I.

questions.questionText: In Meiosis II, the cells that divide are:

options.text: Identical to the original parent cell

questions.explanation: Meiosis II is like mitosis but occurs in haploid cells, separating sister chromatids to produce four haploid gametes.

questions.questionText: Which event contributes most to genetic variation in gametes?
questions.explanation: Crossing over exchanges DNA segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, creating new allele combinations.

questions.questionText: During Anaphase I, what separates?
questions.explanation: In Anaphase I, homologous chromosomes (not sister chromatids) separate and move to opposite poles, reducing chromosome number.

questions.questionText: Chiasmata are:
questions.explanation: Chiasmata are visible X-shaped structures where crossing over occurred between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

questions.questionText: A cell with 2n = 8 chromosomes will produce gametes with how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number. A diploid cell with 8 chromosomes produces haploid gametes with 4 chromosomes each.

questions.questionText: Independent assortment contributes to genetic variation because:

options.text: The way maternal and paternal chromosomes line up is random
Only one type of chromosome is passed on

questions.diagram: Independent assortment during Metaphase I creates different combinations of maternal and paternal chromosomes in gametes, contributing to genetic diversity.

questions.questionText: If an organism has 12 chromosomes (n=6), the number of possible chromosome combinations due to independent assortment is:
questions.explanation: With n=6 (12 chromosomes as 6 homologous pairs), independent assortment can produce 2^6 = 64 different chromosome combinations.

questions.questionText: During Anaphase II, what separates?
questions.explanation: Anaphase II is identical to mitosis - sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles in haploid cells.

questions.questionText: Down syndrome is caused by:
questions.explanation: Down syndrome results from trisomy 21 - three copies of chromosome 21 due to failure of homologous chromosomes to separate during meiosis I.

questions.questionText: Non-disjunction leads to:
questions.diagram: Non-disjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly, producing gametes with abnormal chromosome numbers.

questions.questionText: The difference between meiosis I and meiosis II is:

options.text: Meiosis I halves chromosome number; meiosis II is like mitosis
Both divide the chromosome number equally

questions.explanation: Meiosis I is reductional (halves chromosomes), separating homologues. Meiosis II is equational, separating sister chromatids like mitosis.

questions.questionText: How many genetically distinct types of gametes can a human male produce from independent assortment alone?
questions.diagram: With 23 chromosome pairs, independent assortment alone can produce 2^23 ≈ 8.4 million genetically distinct sperm cells, plus crossing over makes the number even larger.
